verdict: This is a strong, unusually transparent meta-analysis whose descriptive headline — that after correcting for publication bias and model uncertainty the mean incentive-performance partial correlation is near zero in the experimental contexts economists study — is well supported by an above-field-standard correction battery. Two issues dominate the workshop and are corroborated by multiple independent seats. First, the abstract and title generalize into a policy-relevant claim a sample the paper itself describes as curated to avoid contexts where incentives are expected to have large effects (design-stage selection), so the scope qualifier that lives in Section 3 is missing exactly where readers form the takeaway. Second, the headline heterogeneity results (the moderator inclusion ranking and the lab-plus-loss-framing exception) are produced by a Bayesian model averaging exercise the authors concede 'treats all observations as independent,' while the dependence-aware frequentist averaging is relegated to a secondary role. Neither issue overturns the paper; both are addressable by re-emphasis, explicit caveats, and promoting the dependence-aware results. The single positive finding (lab + loss framing, PCC about 0.07) is the most fragile claim and should be re-derived and power-checked before it carries interpretive weight.
top_strengths: The publication-bias and p-hacking correction battery (linear meta-regression plus WAAP/Top10/stem/Andrews-Kasy/kink, MAIVE, p-uniform*, and standard-error-independent caliper/p-curve tests) triangulates across non-overlapping identifying assumptions and is more rigorous than the psychology meta-analyses the paper contrasts itself with.

Model uncertainty is taken seriously with both Bayesian and frequentist model averaging, and the dependence-aware frequentist version (Mallow's weights, study-level clustering) already exists in the paper and can be promoted to anchor the heterogeneity claims.
The paper is candid about its own load-bearing limitations (design-stage selection; the BMA independence assumption) in plain language, and ships its full dataset and code for replication.
The dataset is large and hand-collected (2,193 estimates, 88 experiments, 48 coded moderators), and the search/screening funnel is documented with PRISMA diagrams.

prioritized_findings.one_line: The abstract and title state a general policy claim ('rarely produces large performance gains') without the scope qualifier that the sample is curated to avoid large-effect contexts (design-stage selection); the caveat appears only on p.70.
prioritized_findings.panel_summary: Corroborated by 5 seats (S-DESK-REJECT F-044, S-EXTERNAL-VALIDITY F-057/F-058, S-FRAMING-FATAL F-066/F-068/F-084, S-MISSING-ANALYSIS F-093, generalists F-010). logical-validity upheld; severity High; fix is prose-only (safe to implement).

prioritized_findings.one_line: The headline moderator ranking and Table 5 implied effects come from a BMA that 'treats all observations as independent,' despite 93% of estimates nesting in 88 studies; the dependence-aware frequentist averaging is secondary.
prioritized_findings.panel_summary: Corroborated by 5 seats (S-METHODS-AUDITOR F-086, S-BMA-FATAL F-030, S-PCC-FATAL F-101/F-102, S-HETEROGENEITY-FATAL F-078, S-ROBUSTNESS-CRITIC F-132). logical-validity upheld; severity High; numeric re-emphasis requires an author re-run.

prioritized_findings.one_line: The only positive headline result (lab + loss framing, PCC about 0.07) is a fitted combination of separate marginal effects, not a directly estimated interaction; it straddles the negligible/small threshold, lacks a power/precision analysis, and its framing moderator's inclusion is reported as unstable under alternative priors.
prioritized_findings.panel_summary: Corroborated by 4 seats (S-HETEROGENEITY-FATAL F-078/F-080/F-082, S-MISSING-ANALYSIS F-090, S-PCC-FATAL F-101, S-DESK-REJECT F-048). Specific numeric claims (PIP crossing 0.5; CI endpoints) are marked needs-author-confirmation pending re-run.

prioritized_findings.one_line: MAIVE — the 'preferred' bias-correction estimator anchoring the near-zero framing — is defined inconsistently (body text: inverse sqrt of degrees of freedom; table notes: inverse sqrt of observations), and its exclusion restriction is asserted rather than tested.
prioritized_findings.panel_summary: Corroborated by S-METHODS-AUDITOR (F-085) and S-PUBBIAS-FATAL (F-053/F-120/F-121) and S-DESK-REJECT (F-053). logical-validity upheld; the definition fix is a safe text edit, the exclusion-restriction test requires author work.

prioritized_findings.one_line: The partial correlation coefficient is presented as THE common currency converting incommensurable outcomes, but comparability across the very different primary statistical models (and the sign-harmonization rule) is asserted rather than demonstrated.
prioritized_findings.panel_summary: Corroborated by S-PCC-FATAL (F-103/F-104/F-105) and S-DESK-REJECT (F-046). logical-validity upheld; addressable by reporting PCC distributions by estimation technique and surfacing the harmonization rule from the table footnote.

prioritized_findings.one_line: BMA rigor gaps: the PIP>0.5 inclusion threshold is unmotivated, no MCMC convergence diagnostics are reported for a >30-billion-model space, and a Table B12 robustness check that moves results is downplayed.
prioritized_findings.panel_summary: Corroborated by S-BMA-FATAL (F-026/F-027/F-028) and S-HETEROGENEITY-FATAL (F-080/F-081). Minority report (S-BMA-DEFENSE) notes 0.5 is a standard convention and prior-sensitivity is reported; the gap is justification and convergence reporting, not a fatal flaw.

prioritized_findings.one_line: No inter-coder reliability is reported for the 48 hand-coded moderators (100,000+ data points coded by three co-authors), and the analysis protocol does not state pre-registration.
prioritized_findings.panel_summary: S-DATA-CONSTRUCTION (F-038) and S-MISSING-ANALYSIS (F-092). Absence-silence (quote-exempt); severity High at seat, calibrated toward should-fix transparency; requires author-supplied reliability statistics.

prioritized_findings.one_line: The claim that near-zero average effects are 'not fully consistent with motivation crowding theory' mischaracterizes the theory, which predicts mechanism differences rather than uniform magnitude differences across task types.
prioritized_findings.panel_summary: S-FRAMING-FATAL (F-067/F-069). severity-calibration revised toward Medium (theoretical-interpretation, prose-fixable); minority report (S-FRAMING-DEFENSE) holds the framing is defensible if reworded.

prioritized_findings.one_line: The Doucouliagos (2011) magnitude thresholds (negligible/small/large) are cited in a footnote but not used to consistently interpret what a PCC of 0.05 or 0.07 means substantively for readers from neighboring fields.

kill_shots: This paper dies the way every meta-analysis dies that lets its abstract say more than its design can license: it tells readers 'increasing financial rewards rarely produces large performance gains' while admitting in its own next breath that the literature it pooled was assembled by researchers who 'rarely conduct experiments in contexts where incentives are expected to have large effects because such results are considered trivial' -- so the paper precisely estimates the average size of an effect in a sample explicitly curated to exclude the cases where that effect would be large, and then states the resulting near-zero average as if it were evidence about effect size in general.

The paper's only positive, headline-worthy finding -- the lab-plus-loss-framing effect -- is not a directly estimated interaction but a fitted value combined from separate marginal effects, sitting on the negligible/small boundary, with no power analysis for that thin cell: it is the most-cited number most likely to fail to replicate.

referee_verdicts.verdict: Major revision: the science is sound but the abstract/title overclaim relative to a design-stage-selected sample; fix the framing and the paper is strong.
The correction battery genuinely triangulates and exceeds field norms; residual concern is that MAIVE's exclusion restriction is hedged rather than tested.
The headline heterogeneity rests on an explicitly independence-assuming BMA; promote the dependence-aware averaging and report convergence + threshold justification.
The lab/loss finding is theory-grounded (loss aversion) and survives both Bayesian and frequentist averaging; honest caveats are present, just under-emphasized.
The PCC's status as common currency across heterogeneous designs is assumed, not shown; dependence handling via single-level study clustering is likely insufficient.
Technically exemplary but the contribution is narrower than the abstract implies; the scope limitation should be front-stage, not on p.70.

objections.objection: Abstract/title scope overclaim relative to a design-stage-selected sample.
objections.quote: Our results suggest that increasing financial rewards rarely produces large performance gains in the experimental settings most studied by economists.

objections.objection: Headline heterogeneity rests on an independence-assuming BMA while a dependence-aware method exists in the paper.
objections.quote: The Bayesian approach, however, treats all observations as independent, and to account for within-study dependence we also employ frequentist model averaging with Mallow's weights (Hansen, 2007) and orthogonalization of model space according to Amini & Parmeter (2012).

objections.objection: The 'preferred' bias-correction instrument's exclusion restriction is asserted, not tested.
objections.quote: Such an instrument is correlated with the standard error by the definition of the latter and can be expected to be less related to method choices.

venue_verdict.swing_factor: Whether the abstract/conclusion carry the design-stage-selection scope qualifier and whether the dependence-aware model-averaging results are promoted to anchor the heterogeneity claims (with the lab+loss exception re-derived and power-checked). These are emphasis/transparency changes, not new science.

validity_verdict: The central descriptive claim — that after a thorough publication-bias and model-uncertainty correction the mean incentive-performance PCC is near zero across the studied experimental contexts — is supported by the data and an unusually complete correction battery. What is not fully licensed by the design is (a) the broader policy generalization, because the pooled literature is, by the authors' own account, selected to avoid large-effect contexts, and (b) the robustness of the single positive exception (lab + loss framing), which is a fitted, threshold-straddling, dependence-naive quantity. The validity verdict therefore dominates the venue read: the paper is publishable and strong, but its headline sentence and its one positive result should be re-scoped and re-derived.
minority_report: A substantial defender position (S-PUBBIAS-DEFENSE, S-BMA-DEFENSE, S-HETEROGENEITY-DEFENSE, S-FRAMING-DEFENSE) holds that several 'fatal' framings are better read as emphasis and transparency fixes than validity failures: the bias-correction battery and dual model-averaging genuinely triangulate; the design-stage-selection caveat and the BMA independence assumption ARE disclosed (just not foregrounded); the lab/loss result is grounded in established loss-aversion theory rather than pure data-dredging; and the PIP>0.5 cutoff is a standard convention (Eicher et al. 2011; Steel 2020). On this reading the paper needs re-scoping, not re-doing.

rejected_suggestions.suggestion: The paper offers no actionable practitioner guidance (G-CROSS-FIELD F-001).
rejected_suggestions.why_rejected: logical-validity panel: prescriptive practitioner guidance is outside the scope of an effect-size meta-analysis; not a validity defect.

rejected_suggestions.suggestion: The design-stage-selection caveat makes the contribution near-pointless (G-CROSS-FIELD F-002).
rejected_suggestions.why_rejected: logical-validity panel: misreads the paper, which discusses lab-vs-field and framing heterogeneity throughout; the contribution stands once scoped.

rejected_suggestions.suggestion: The paper should add a cost-benefit analysis of incentive implementation (G-RELEVANCE F-007).
rejected_suggestions.why_rejected: logical-validity panel: beyond the remit of a meta-analysis of experimental effect sizes.

rejected_suggestions.suggestion: PCC standardization across tasks is uninterpretable (G-UNDERSTANDABILITY F-011).
rejected_suggestions.why_rejected: logical-validity panel: PCC is a well-established meta-analytic currency; the real, narrower issue (comparability across statistical models) is retained as F-105.

rejected_suggestions.suggestion: The paper never explains why lab effects differ from field effects (G-UNDERSTANDABILITY F-015).
rejected_suggestions.why_rejected: logical-validity panel: the paper offers the distraction-effect explanation (Rusz et al. 2020); the finding misreads the text.

rejected_suggestions.suggestion: Table 2 quantitative results undercut the MAIVE framing / the paper never says when incentives work (S-PUBBIAS-FATAL F-122).
rejected_suggestions.why_rejected: logical-validity panel: the paper does analyze task-characteristic interactions; the narrower MAIVE-definition and exclusion-restriction points are retained as F-085/F-053/F-121.
